correctness.rationale: In a window of length divisible by four the odd positions alternate and contribute exactly one quarter of the total length as ones. The evens decimate to a contiguous shorter window. Iterating to length two gives K=N/2-1+p_J+p_(J+1), J=ceil(t/(N/2)). Successive odd-indexed symbols are complementary, so each odd-start pair of adjacency edges contributes exactly one transition. The N-1 edges contain (N-2)/2 complete such pairs and one lone edge, with the latter at the first or last position according to starting parity. Endpoint parity therefore fixes T to N/2 or N/2-1. At fixed N, K, the endpoints and T determine all four bigram counts, and those counts with K recover both endpoints using their sum and difference. For k>=4, the starts (J-1)N/2+d for J=1,3,11 and d=2,3,4,7 all use the designated J above. The leading offset is divisible by 16; checking residues modulo 4, 8 or 16 gives the four claimed endpoint pairs at every J. Direct evaluation confirms the twelve starts at N=8. A separate bounded generation of the word and literal bigram census found exactly twelve distinct full profiles for lengths 8 through 256 within the sampled starts and reproduced the N=8 witnesses. The general edge and witness arguments, not the finite prefix samples, establish the all-length theorem.
residual_risks: The bounded prefix tests are not an exhaustion of the infinite word. The exact proof treats the given regular word and dyadic lengths at least eight, not other lengths or folding instruction sequences.

evidence: Madill–Rampersad give rho(2)=3 and rho(4n)=rho(2n) for ordinary Abelian complexity. The universal dyadic Abelian catalogue result establishes these weight layers for every folding instruction sequence. The two 2-Abelian recurrence treatments cover other words.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Generalizing the family of folding words at Abelian order one still does not decide which first/last letters coexist with each weight. The recurrences for other words cannot be substituted into a different input sequence.

originality.rationale: The three ordinary Abelian weight classes at dyadic lengths are prior work. The inspected consecutive-pair literature specializes to other automatic words, while the closest paperfolding records count weights, cyclic rotations or scattered two-letter subsequences. The supported distinct claim is the complete endpoint refinement of each weight layer for contiguous bigram equivalence, and hence the twelve classes.
residual_risks: A bounded search cannot rule out an unindexed or implicitly equivalent paperfolding recurrence. No conclusion about priority is drawn from catalogue dates.

value.rationale: Powers of two match the word's even-position self-similarity and are a natural regime rather than sampled lengths. The pair-count level is the first refinement beyond the known Abelian weight count. The result gives the exact class count and a full weight/endpoint description with uniform witnesses, useful as an exact benchmark for 2-Abelian complexity of this standard automatic word.
residual_risks: This does not give the full nondyadic complexity sequence or classify the larger family of paperfolding words at Abelian order two.
